findings.expected: Use a French banner (banner-fr.png) with "Un financement adapté à vos projets / Taux concurrentiels. Modalités claires. Aucune surprise."
findings.description: The French landing page displays the English banner image containing English text "Financing that fits your plans / Competitive rates. Clear terms. No surprises."
The site footer is in English on French pages.
The subtitle uses "tu" while the title just above and the rest of the site use "vous".
"Appliquer pour" is a well-known anglicism (calque of "apply for") flagged by the OQLF; "faire une demande de prêt" or "Demander un prêt" is correct.
The required-field error for "Nom complet" is shown in English, while the other fields' errors are translated.

findings.expected: Let the button grow with its content (remove fixed width / overflow hidden), or shorten to "Soumettre la demande".
findings.description: The French submit button label is clipped to "Soumettre ma demande" (scrollWidth 290 > clientWidth 210, overflow hidden, nowrap).
"e-mail" is not standard in Canadian French; the OQLF recommends "courriel" / "adresse courriel".

findings.expected: Parse the amount with fr-CA conventions (comma as decimal separator, space/narrow no-break space as thousands separator).
findings.description: On the French form, amounts entered in French format ("12 500,50" or "12500,50") are rejected as out of range, even though the error message itself uses French formatting; French users cannot enter amounts naturally.

findings.observed: Merci. Votre demande pour {montant} a été reçue.
findings.expected: Merci. Votre demande de 12 500,00 $ a été reçue.
findings.description: The French confirmation shows the raw template variable {montant} instead of the amount; the variable name was likely translated so it no longer matches the interpolation key.
The transactions section heading is left in English on the French dashboard.
Transaction dates on the French dashboard use US MM/DD/YYYY format, which is not a fr-CA convention and is ambiguous (the English page uses ISO).
"Balance" for an account balance is an anglicism in Quebec banking; the correct term is "solde".
A bank "statement" is a "relevé" in French; "déclaration" means a declaration (e.g. tax return), which changes the meaning.
The "Estimer un nouveau prêt" link on the French dashboard points to the English calculator, switching the user to English.
In French, zero takes the singular; the English plural rule was applied ("0 prêts actifs").
The option "Pay later" (first payment deferred) is translated as "Payer maintenant" (pay now), the opposite meaning, contradicting its own help text.
The estimated monthly payment on the French calculator uses English currency formatting.

findings.observed: Aucune accusation pour un remboursement anticipé.
findings.expected: Aucuns frais pour un remboursement anticipé.
findings.description: "Charges" (fees) was translated as "accusation" (criminal charge), which is wrong in context.

findings.expected: Taux variable de 5,2 %, sous réserve de l'approbation du crédit.
findings.description: The French drops the condition "subject to credit approval", presenting the rate as unconditional.

findings.expected: Use the French version of promo-a showing "Taux variable : 5,2 %".
findings.description: The French page shows a different promo image advertising a fixed rate of 4.9%, contradicting its alt text and the English page's variable 5.2% rate.
The dialog's "Close" action was translated as the adjective "Proche" (near) instead of the verb "Fermer".

findings.observed: Not Found — The requested URL was not found on the server. If you entered the URL manually please check your spelling and try again.
findings.expected: Provide a localized 404 page: "Page introuvable — La page demandée n'existe pas." with lang="fr-CA".
findings.description: Unknown URLs under /fr/ show the server's default English 404 page (html lang="en").
The French application confirmation page declares html lang="en" although its content is French.
